P.h: X.com web app rebuilt by five engineers and AI coding agents
P.p: The new X.com web app was built by five engineers working with AI coding agents in under six months. It loads pages significantly faster than the old app over slow connections, and already serves logged-out users and the pages search engines crawl.
P.s: The post covers why X was rebuilt, how the rollout works, and how old and new apps compare. Separately, a post argues teams must be choosier about which bugs to fix, since fixing everything is no longer practical.

items.d: Rolling out globally in ChatGPT and Codex. Images generate 50% faster, GIFs can be edited frame by frame, and GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst reach the API.

items.h: Apple cuts internal AI spending caps
items.d: Some engineers drop from $300 to $200 a day, with further cuts to as low as $100 planned. Non-engineering groups may fall to $25. Few staff used the full cap.

items.h: US AI capacity hits an 81 GW ceiling in 2027
items.d: Capacity grows from 38 GW today. Data-center power is the constraint.

items.h: Top 1% of AI spenders stalled in Q3
items.d: Anthropic's dollar growth stalled too, while adoption at all other firms keeps rising.

tiles.d: Nearly every local ballot measure opposing data centers won or is winning. AI scarcity may last longer than expected.
